contents.html: Since applications will depend upon the identity established during this process, it is crucial that appropriate procedures for the validation of identity (i.e., identity proofing) be established and used. Identity proofing is often performed by an organization (e.g., by the organization’s security office) but may also be performed by a registration authority for the key management system. The strength (or weakness) of a security infrastructure will often depend upon the identification process. FIPS 20192 and SP 800-6393 address requirements for establishing identity.
contents.html_ja: アプリケーションはこのプロセスで確立された識別情報に依存するため、識別情報の検証（すなわち身元確認）のための適切な手順を確立し、使用することが極めて重要である。身元確認は組織（たとえば、組織のセキュリティ部署）によって実施されることが多いが、鍵管理システムの登録機関によって実施されることもある。セキュリティ基盤の強度（または脆弱性）は、多くの場合、識別プロセスに左右される。FIPS 20192およびSP 800-6393は、識別情報の確立に関する要件を扱っている。

contents.html: Entity and key registration (see Section 8.1.6) may be performed separately or in concert. If performed separately, the entity registration process will generally establish a secret value (e.g., a password, PIN, or HMAC key); the secret value may be used to authenticate the entity’s identity during the key-registration step. If performed in concert, the entity establishes an identity and performs key registration in the same process, so the secret value is not required.
contents.html_ja: エンティティ登録と鍵登録（8.1.6節を参照）は、別々に行うことも、一体として行うこともできる。別々に行う場合、エンティティ登録プロセスでは通常、秘密値（たとえば、パスワード、PIN、またはHMAC鍵）が確立される。この秘密値は、鍵登録の段階でエンティティの識別情報を認証するために使用されることがある。一体として行う場合、エンティティは同一のプロセスで識別情報を確立し鍵登録を行うため、秘密値は必要ない。

contents.html: 92 FIPS 201, Personal Identity Verification (PIV) of Federal Employees and Contractors.
contents.html_ja: 92 FIPS 201, Personal Identity Verification (PIV) of Federal Employees and Contractors.

contents.html: 93 SP 800-63, Digital Identity Guidelines.
contents.html_ja: 93 SP 800-63, Digital Identity Guidelines.

contents.html: 8.1.2 System Initialization Function
contents.html_ja: 8.1.2 システム初期化機能

contents.html: System initialization involves setting up or configuring a system for secure operation. For systems handling keys, this may include algorithm preferences, the identification of trusted parties, and the definition of domain-parameter policies and any trusted parameters (e.g., recognized certificate policies).
contents.html_ja: システム初期化では、安全に運用できるようシステムを設定または構成する。鍵を扱うシステムでは、これにアルゴリズムの優先設定、信頼する関係者の識別、ドメインパラメータポリシーおよび信頼するパラメータ（例：認識済みの証明書ポリシー）の定義などが含まれる場合がある。

contents.html: 8.1.3 Initialization Function
contents.html_ja: 8.1.3 初期化機能

contents.html: Initialization consists of an entity initializing its cryptographic application (e.g., installing and initializing software or hardware). This involves the use or installation (see Section 8.1.4) of the initial keying material that may be obtained during entity registration. Examples include the installation of a key at a CA, trust parameters, policies, trusted parties, and algorithm preferences.
contents.html_ja: 初期化とは、エンティティが暗号アプリケーションを初期化すること（例：ソフトウェアまたはハードウェアのインストールと初期設定）である。これには、エンティティ登録中に取得されることがある初期鍵素材の使用またはインストール（8.1.4節を参照）が含まれる。例として、CAへの鍵のインストール、信頼パラメータ、ポリシー、信頼する関係者、アルゴリズムの優先設定がある。

contents.html: 8.1.4 Keying-Material Installation Function
contents.html_ja: 8.1.4 鍵素材インストール機能

contents.html: The security of keying-material installation is crucial to the security of a system, whether the keying material is generated within the system (e.g., in the system’s cryptographic module) or generated within another system and subsequently installed in the (target) system. For this function, keying material is installed for operational use within an entity’s software, hardware, system, application, cryptographic module, or device using a variety of techniques. Keying material is installed during initial setup when new keying material is added to the existing keying material and the existing keying material is replaced (e.g., via re-keying or key derivation; see Sections 8.2.3 and 8.2.4).
contents.html_ja: 鍵材料のインストールのセキュリティは、鍵材料がシステム内（たとえば、システムの暗号モジュール内）で生成される場合であれ、別のシステム内で生成されてから（対象）システムにインストールされる場合であれ、システムのセキュリティにとって極めて重要である。この機能では、さまざまな手法を用いて、エンティティのソフトウェア、ハードウェア、システム、アプリケーション、暗号モジュール、またはデバイス内に運用のための鍵材料をインストールする。鍵材料は、初期セットアップ時、既存の鍵材料に新しい鍵材料が追加されるとき、および既存の鍵材料が置換されるとき（たとえば、再鍵化または鍵導出による。8.2.3節および8.2.4節を参照）にインストールされる。

contents.html: The process for the initial installation of keying material (e.g., by manual entry, using an electronic key loader, or a vendor during manufacture) shall include the protection of the keying material during entry into a software, hardware, system, application, device, or cryptographic module − taking into account the requirements of FIPS 140 and its differing requirements for the different levels of protection − and include any additional procedures that may be required.
contents.html_ja: 鍵材料の初期インストールのプロセス（たとえば、手入力、電子的な鍵ローダーの使用、または製造時のベンダーによるもの）には、ソフトウェア、ハードウェア、システム、アプリケーション、デバイス、または暗号モジュールへの入力時における鍵材料の保護を含めなければならない。その際、FIPS 140の要件と、保護レベルごとに異なるその要件を考慮しなければならない。さらに、必要となる追加の手順も含めなければならない。

contents.html: Many applications or systems are provided by the manufacturer with keying material that is used to test that the newly installed application/system is functioning properly. This test keying material shall not be used operationally.
contents.html_ja: 多くのアプリケーションやシステムは、新たにインストールされたアプリケーション／システムが正しく機能していることをテストするために使用する鍵材料とともに、製造者から提供される。このテスト用鍵材料を運用に使用してはならない。

contents.html: 8.1.5 Key Establishment Function
contents.html_ja: 8.1.5 鍵確立機能

contents.html: Key establishment involves the generation and distribution or the agreement of keying material for communication between entities. All keys shall be generated within a FIPS 140-validated cryptographic module or obtained from another source approved by the U.S. Government for the protection of national security information. Long-term keys shall be inventoried (see Section 9.2). During the key-establishment process, some of the keying material may be in transit (i.e., the keying material is being manually distributed or is being distributed using automated protocols). Other keying material may be retained locally rather than distributed. In either case, the keying material shall be protected in accordance with Section 6.
contents.html_ja: 鍵確立には、エンティティ間の通信のための鍵材料の生成と配布、または合意が含まれる。すべての鍵は、FIPS 140の認証を受けた暗号モジュール内で生成するか、国家安全保障情報の保護のために米国政府が承認した他の供給源から入手しなければならない。長期鍵はインベントリに登録しなければならない（9.2節を参照）。鍵確立プロセスの間、鍵材料の一部は転送中である（すなわち、鍵材料が手動で配布されているか、自動化されたプロトコルを用いて配布されている）ことがある。その他の鍵材料は、配布されずにローカルに保持されることがある。いずれの場合も、鍵材料は第6章に従って保護しなければならない。

contents.html: An entity may be an individual (human), organization, device, or process. When keying material is generated by an entity for its own use, one or more of the appropriate protection mechanisms for stored information in Section 6.2.2 shall be used. The “owner” of a key is an entity that is authorized to use the key. When the owner is not a human (i.e., the owner is an organization, device, or process), the owner is often assisted by an authorized human representative or sponsor to obtain and manage keying material (e.g., to obtain and install keys and certificates).
contents.html_ja: エンティティは、個人（人間）、組織、デバイス、またはプロセスでありうる。エンティティが自ら使用するために鍵材料を生成する場合は、6.2.2節に示す保存情報に対する適切な保護メカニズムのうち一つ以上を使用しなければならない。鍵の「所有者」とは、その鍵の使用を認可されたエンティティである。所有者が人間でない場合（すなわち、所有者が組織、デバイス、またはプロセスである場合）、所有者は多くの場合、鍵材料の入手と管理（たとえば、鍵と証明書の入手とインストール）について、認可された人間の代表者またはスポンサーの支援を受ける。

contents.html: Keying material that is distributed between entities or among an entity and its sub-entities (e.g., various individuals, devices, or processes within an organization) shall be protected during distribution using one or more of the appropriate protection mechanisms specified in Section 6.2.1. Any keying material that is not distributed (e.g., the private key of a key pair or one’s own copy of a symmetric key) or keying material that is received and subsequently stored shall be protected using one or more of the appropriate protection mechanisms specified in Section 6.2.2.
contents.html_ja: エンティティ間、またはエンティティとそのサブエンティティ（たとえば、組織内のさまざまな個人、デバイス、またはプロセス）との間で配布される鍵材料は、配布中、6.2.1節に規定された適切な保護メカニズムのうち一つ以上を用いて保護しなければならない。配布されない鍵材料（たとえば、鍵ペアの私有鍵や、自身が保持する対称鍵のコピー）、または受信された後に保存される鍵材料は、6.2.2節に規定された適切な保護メカニズムのうち一つ以上を用いて保護しなければならない。

contents.html: Sections 8.1.5.1 and 8.1.5.2 discuss the generation and distribution of asymmetric and symmetric keys, respectively. SP 800-133 discusses the generation of keying material.
contents.html_ja: 8.1.5.1節および8.1.5.2節では、それぞれ非対称鍵および対称鍵の生成と配布について述べる。SP 800-133では鍵材料の生成について述べている。

contents.html: 8.1.5.1 Generation and Distribution of Asymmetric Key Pairs
contents.html_ja: 8.1.5.1 非対称鍵ペアの生成と配布

contents.html: Key pairs shall be generated in accordance with the mathematical specifications of the appropriate approved FIPS or NIST Recommendation.
contents.html_ja: 鍵ペアは、適切な承認済みのFIPSまたはNIST勧告の数学的仕様に従って生成しなければならない。

contents.html: A static key pair shall be generated by either: 1) the entity that owns the key pair (i.e., the entity that uses the private key in the cryptographic computations), 2) a facility that distributes the key pair in accordance with Section 8.1.5.1.3, or 3) the owner and facility in a cooperative process.
contents.html_ja: 静的鍵ペアは、次のいずれかによって生成しなければならない。1) 鍵ペアを所有するエンティティ（すなわち、暗号計算において私有鍵を使用するエンティティ）、2) 8.1.5.1.3節に従って鍵ペアを配布する施設、または3) 所有者と施設の協調プロセス。

contents.html: In the case of a digital signature key pair (a public signature-verification key and its associated private key), the owner of the static key pair should generate the keying material rather than any other entity generating the keying material for that owner; this will facilitate support for non-repudiation. When generated by the entity that owns the key pair, a private signature key shall not be distributed to other entities. However, when the owner is an organization, it is acceptable to distribute the keying material to the organization’s sub-entities (e.g., employees or devices); in this case, the organization is the true owner, and the sub-entities represent the owner.
contents.html_ja: デジタル署名鍵ペア（公開署名検証鍵とそれに対応する秘密鍵）の場合、静的鍵ペアの所有者が鍵材料を生成すべきであり、他のエンティティが所有者に代わって生成すべきではない。これにより否認防止の支援が容易になる。鍵ペアを所有するエンティティが生成した場合、秘密署名鍵を他のエンティティに配布してはならない。ただし、所有者が組織である場合は、鍵材料を組織の下位エンティティ（例えば従業員やデバイス）に配布してもよい。この場合、組織が真の所有者であり、下位エンティティは所有者を代表する。

contents.html: Ephemeral keys are often used for key agreement instead of or in addition to the use of static keys (see SP 800-56A). Ephemeral key pairs are generated for each new key-establishment transaction (e.g., unique to each message or session) by the owner.
contents.html_ja: 鍵合意では、静的鍵の代わりに、または静的鍵に加えて、エフェメラル鍵がしばしば用いられる（SP 800-56Aを参照）。エフェメラル鍵ペアは、新たな鍵確立トランザクションごとに（例えばメッセージごとまたはセッションごとに固有のものとして）所有者が生成する。

contents.html: The generated key pairs shall be protected in accordance with Section 6.1.1.
contents.html_ja: 生成した鍵ペアは、6.1.1節に従って保護しなければならない。

contents.html: 8.1.5.1.1 Distribution of Public Keys
contents.html_ja: 8.1.5.1.1 公開鍵の配布

contents.html: Static public keys are relatively long-lived and are typically used for several executions of an algorithm. Ephemeral public keys are short-lived. The distribution of the static or ephemeral public key should provide assurance to the receiver of the public key that the true owner of the key is known (i.e., the claimed owner is the actual owner); this requirement may be disregarded if anonymity is acceptable. However, the strength of the overall architecture and trust in the validity of the protected data depends, in large part, on assurance of the public-key owner’s identity.
contents.html_ja: 静的公開鍵は比較的長期間使用され、通常はアルゴリズムの複数回の実行に用いられる。エフェメラル公開鍵の使用期間は短い。静的公開鍵またはエフェメラル公開鍵の配布は、公開鍵の受信者に対し、鍵の真の所有者が判明していること（すなわち、主張された所有者が実際の所有者であること）の保証を与えるべきである。匿名性が許容される場合は、この要件を考慮しなくてもよい。ただし、アーキテクチャ全体の強度と保護されたデータの正当性に対する信頼は、公開鍵所有者の識別情報の保証に大きく依存する。

contents.html: In addition, the distribution of the public key shall provide assurance to the receiver that:
contents.html_ja: さらに、公開鍵の配布は、受信者に対して次の事項を保証しなければならない。

contents.html: The purpose/usage of the key is known (e.g., for RSA digital signatures or elliptic-curve key agreement);
contents.html_ja: 鍵の目的／使用法が既知であること（例：RSAデジタル署名または楕円曲線鍵共有用）。

contents.html: Any parameters associated with the public key are known (e.g., domain parameters);
contents.html_ja: 公開鍵に関連するパラメータが既知であること（例：ドメインパラメータ）。

contents.html: The public key is valid (e.g., the public key satisfies the required arithmetical properties); and
contents.html_ja: 公開鍵が有効であること（例：公開鍵が必要な算術的性質を満たす）。

contents.html: The owner actually possesses the corresponding private key.
contents.html_ja: 所有者が対応する秘密鍵を実際に所持していること。

contents.html: 8.1.5.1.1.1 Distribution of a Trust Anchor’s Public Key in a PKI
contents.html_ja: 8.1.5.1.1.1 PKIにおけるトラストアンカー公開鍵の配布

contents.html: The public key of a trusted Certification Authority is the foundation for all PKI-based security services; the trusted CA is considered to be a trust anchor. The trust anchor’s public key is not a secret, but the authenticity of that public key is the crucial assumption for a PKI. Trust anchor public keys may be obtained through many different mechanisms, providing different levels of assurance. The types of mechanisms that are provided may depend on the role of the entity in the infrastructure. An entity that only ever acts as a “relying party” – that is, an entity that does not have keys registered with the infrastructure – may use different mechanisms than an entity that possesses keys registered by the infrastructure.

Trust-anchor public keys are frequently distributed as root-CA certificates − “self-signed” X.509 certificates that are signed by the private key corresponding to the public key in the certificate. Note that, while this document refers to a trusted CA as the “trust anchor” and its certificate as the “trust-anchor certificate,” many other documents use the term “trust anchor” to refer to both the trusted CA and the CA’s certificate.

Trust-anchor certificates are often embedded within an application and distributed with the application. For example, the installation of a new web browser typically includes the installation or replacement of the entity’s list of trust-anchor certificates. Operating systems are usually shipped with trust-anchor certificates for a variety of reasons, including the validation of other certificates. The entity relies upon the authenticity of the software distribution mechanism to ensure that only valid trust-anchor certificates are installed during installation or replacement. However, in some cases, other applications may install trust-anchor certificates in web browsers.

Trust-anchor certificates in web browsers are used for several purposes, including the validation of the TLS certificates presented in TLS protocols. Entities that visit a “secure” website that has a certificate that was not issued by a trust anchor CA may be given an opportunity to accept that certificate, either for a single session or permanently. Relying parties should be cautious about accepting certificates from unknown Certification Authorities so that they do not, in effect, inadvertently add new permanent trust-anchor certificates that are really not trustworthy.

Warning: Roaming users should be aware that they are implicitly trusting all software on the host systems that they use. They should have concerns about trust-anchor certificates used by web browsers when they use systems in kiosks, libraries, internet cafes, or hotels as well as systems provided by conference organizers to access “secure websites.” The user has had no control over the trust-anchor certificates installed in the host system, and therefore, the user is relying upon the host system administrators to have made good, sensible decisions about which trust-anchor certificates are allowed. Relying parties are not participants in trust-anchor certificate selection when the trust-anchor certificates are pre-installed prior to software distribution and may have had no part in decisions about which trust-anchor certificates are installed thereafter. The users should be aware that they are trusting the software distribution mechanism to not have resulted in the installation of malicious code. Extending this trust to cover trust-anchor certificates for a given application may be reasonable and allows the relying party to obtain trust-anchor certificates without any additional procedures.

The entity (or the entity’s representative) interacts securely with the infrastructure to register its keys (e.g., to obtain certificates), and these interactions may be extended to provide trust-anchor information in the form of a trust-anchor certificate. This allows the establishment of trust-anchor certificates with approximately the same assurance that the infrastructure has in the entity’s keys. In the case of a PKI:

1. The initial distribution of a trust-anchor certificate should be performed in conjunction with the presentation of a requesting entity’s public key to a registration authority (RA) or CA during the certificate-request process. In general, the trust anchor’s public key, associated parameters, key use, and assurance of possession are conveyed as a self-signed X.509 public-key certificate (also called a root-CA certificate). In this case, the certificate has been digitally signed by the private key that corresponds to the public key within the certificate. While the parameters and assurance of possession may be conveyed in the self-signed certificate, the identity associated with the trust-anchor certificate and other information cannot be verified from the self-signed certificate itself (see item 2 below).

The trusted process used to convey a requesting entity’s public key and assurances to the RA or CA shall also be used to protect the trust-anchor’s certificate that is conveyed to the requesting entity. In cases where the requesting entity (or the entity’s representative) appears in person, the trust-anchor’s certificate may be provided at that time. If a secret value has been established during entity registration (see Section 8.1.1), the trust-anchor’s certificate may be supplied along with the requesting entity’s certificate.
contents.html_ja: 要求エンティティの公開鍵と保証をRAまたはCAへ伝達するために使用する信頼済みプロセスを、要求エンティティに伝達するトラストアンカー証明書の保護にも使用しなければならない。要求エンティティ（またはその代表者）が対面で手続きする場合、その時点でトラストアンカー証明書を提供してよい。エンティティ登録中に秘密値を確立している場合（8.1.1節を参照）、要求エンティティの証明書と共にトラストアンカー証明書を提供してよい。

contents.html: 8.1.5.1.1.2 Submission to a Registration Authority or Certification Authority
contents.html_ja: 8.1.5.1.1.2 登録局または認証局への提出

contents.html: Public keys may be provided to a Certification Authority (CA) or registration authority (RA) for subsequent certification by a CA. During this process, the RA or CA shall obtain the assurances listed in Section 8.1.5.1.1 and the owner’s identity from the entity submitting the key (i.e., the owner of the key or an authorized representative).

In general, the owner of the key is identified in terms of an identifier established during entity registration (see Section 8.1.1). During entity registration, the appropriate uses for the key are identified along with any required parameters. In cases where anonymous ownership of the public key is acceptable, the submitter or the registration authority determines a pseudonym to be used as the identifier. The identifier shall be unique for the naming authority.94

Proof of possession (POP) is a mechanism that is commonly used by a CA to obtain assurance of private-key possession during key registration. In this case, the proof shall be provided by the reputed owner of the key pair. Without assurance of possession, it would be possible for the CA to bind the public key to the wrong entity.

The (reputed) owner should provide POP by performing operations with the private key that satisfy the indicated key use. For example, if a key pair is intended for RSA digital signature generation, the CA may provide information to be signed using the owner’s private key. If the CA can correctly verify the signature using the corresponding public key, then the owner has established POP. However, when a key pair is intended to support key establishment (i.e., either key agreement or key transport), and the key pair was generated as specified in FIPS 18695 (see

94 The naming authority is the entity responsible for the allocation and distribution of domain names, ensuring that the names are unique within the domain. A naming authority is often restricted to a particular level of domains, such as .com, .net, or .edu.
contents.html_ja: 94 ネーミング機関とは、ドメイン名の割当てと配布を担い、ドメイン内で名前が一意となることを保証する主体である。ネーミング機関は、.com、.net、.eduなど、特定の階層のドメインに限定されることが多い。

contents.html: 95 SP 800-56A also allows the use of predefined groups for finite-field Diffie-Hellman key agreement. POP cannot be performed using a digital signature when these parameters are used. SP 800-56A and SP 800-56B), POP may also be afforded by using the private key to digitally sign the certificate request (although this is not the preferred method). The private key-establishment key (i.e., the private key-agreement or private key-transport key) shall not be used to perform signature operations after certificate issuance.

page_check.proof_note: Footnote 95 printed on this page ends at 'when these parameters are used.'; the remaining text ('SP 800-56A and SP 800-56B), POP may also be afforded...') is body text of the paragraph (block 11) continuing on the next page, not footnote text.

contents.html: As with entity registration, the strength of the security infrastructure depends upon the methods used for distributing the key to an RA or CA. There are many different methods, each appropriate for some range of applications. Some examples of common methods are:

The public key and the information identified in Section 8.1.5.1.1 are provided in person by the public-key owner or by an authorized representative of the public-key owner (e.g., an organization, device, or process).
contents.html_ja: 公開鍵と8.1.5.1.1節で特定する情報は、公開鍵所有者または公開鍵所有者の許可された代理人（例：組織、デバイス、プロセス）が直接（対面で）提供する。

contents.html: The identity of the public-key owner or an authorized representative of the public-key owner is established and their authorization verified in person by the RA or CA during entity registration. Unique, unpredictable information (e.g., an authenticator or cryptographic key) is provided at this time by the RA or CA to the owner or authorized representative as a secret value. The information identified in Section 8.1.5.1.1 and the public key are provided to the RA or CA using a communication protocol protected by the secret value. As specified in Section 8.3.4, the secret value should be destroyed by the key owner or owner’s representative upon receiving confirmation that the certificate has been successfully generated. The RA or CA may maintain this secret value for auditing purposes, but the RA or CA should not accept further use of the secret value to prove identity.
contents.html_ja: エンティティ登録時に、公開鍵所有者または公開鍵所有者の権限を与えられた代理人の身元を確立し、その権限をRAまたはCAが対面で確認する。RAまたはCAはこの時点で、一意で予測不能な情報（例：認証器や暗号鍵）を秘密値として所有者または権限を与えられた代理人に提供する。8.1.5.1.1節で示す情報と公開鍵は、この秘密値で保護した通信プロトコルを用いてRAまたはCAに提供する。8.3.4節に規定するとおり、証明書が正常に生成されたことの確認を受けた時点で、鍵所有者または所有者の代理人は秘密値を破棄するべきである。RAまたはCAは監査目的でこの秘密値を保持してもよいが、RAまたはCAは、身元の証明のためにこの秘密値をその後も使用することを受け入れるべきではない。

contents.html: When a specific list of public-key owners is preauthorized to register keys, identifiers may be assigned without the owners being present. In this case, it is critical to protect the secret values from disclosure, and the procedures shall demonstrate that the chain of custody was maintained. The lifetime of the secret values should be limited but shall allow for the public-key owner or the owner’s representative to appear at the RA or CA, generate the keys, and provide the public key (under the secret value’s protection) to the RA or CA. Since it may take some time for the public-key owner or owner’s representative to appear at the RA or CA, a two or three-week lifetime for the secret value is probably reasonable.

When public-key owners are not preauthorized, the RA or CA shall determine the identifier in the presence of the owner or representative. In this case, the time limit may be much more restrictive if the key pair is generated on-site and the public key is provided to the CA or RA. In this case, a 24-hour lifetime for the secret value would be reasonable.

3. The identity of the public-key owner is established at the RA or CA using a previous determination of the public-key owner’s identity; the continued authorization to receive a certificate is also verified. Recertification involves “chaining” a new public-key certificate request to a previously certified digital-signature key pair. For example, the request for a new public-key certificate is signed by the owner of the new public key to be certified. The private signature key used to sign the request should correspond to a public signature-verification key that was certified by the same CA that will certify the new public key. The request contains the new public key and any key-related information (e.g., the key use and the key’s parameters). In addition, the CA shall obtain assurance of public-key validity and assurance that the owner possesses the corresponding private key.

The public key, key use, parameters, validity assurance information, and assurance of possession are provided to the RA or CA along with a claimed identity for the owner and the authorization to receive a certificate. The RA or CA delegates the verification of the public-key owner’s identity and authorization to another trusted process (e.g., an examination of the public-key owner’s identity by the U.S. Postal Service when delivering registered mail containing the requested certificate). Upon receiving a request for certification, the RA or CA generates and sends unique, unpredictable information (e.g., an authenticator or cryptographic key) to the requestor using a trusted process (e.g., registered mail sent via the U.S. Postal Service). The trusted process assures that the identity of the requestor is verified prior to delivery of the information provided by the RA or CA. The owner or owner’s representative uses this information to prove that the trusted process succeeded, and the RA or CA subsequently delivers the certificate to the owner or the owner’s representative. As specified in Section 8.3.4, the unique, unpredictable information should be destroyed by the key owner or representative upon receiving confirmation that the certificate has been successfully generated. (The RA or CA may maintain this information for auditing purposes but should not accept further use of the unique identifier to prove identity.)
contents.html_ja: 公開鍵、鍵の用途、パラメータ、有効性保証情報、および所持の保証は、所有者の申告された身元および証明書を受け取る権限とともにRAまたはCAに提供する。RAまたはCAは、公開鍵所有者の身元と権限の確認を別の信頼できるプロセスに委任する（例：要求された証明書を含む書留郵便を配達する際に、米国郵便公社が公開鍵所有者の身元を確認する）。証明の要求を受けると、RAまたはCAは、信頼できるプロセス（例：米国郵便公社を通じた書留郵便）を用いて、一意で予測不能な情報（例：認証器や暗号鍵）を生成して要求者に送る。この信頼できるプロセスにより、RAまたはCAが提供する情報を配達する前に要求者の身元が確認されることが保証される。所有者または所有者の代理人はこの情報を用いて、信頼できるプロセスが成功したことを証明し、その後RAまたはCAは証明書を所有者または所有者の代理人に配達する。8.3.4節に規定するとおり、証明書が正常に生成されたことの確認を受けた時点で、鍵所有者または代理人は、この一意で予測不能な情報を破棄するべきである。（RAまたはCAは監査目的でこの情報を保持してもよいが、身元の証明のために一意の識別子をその後も使用することを受け入れるべきではない。）

contents.html: The public key and Domain Name System (DNS) address(es) to be included in the common name or subject alternative name(s) of the certificate are provided over a network connection to the RA via a certificate signing request. The RA confirms that the requestor is authorized to request a certificate for the DNS address(es) by performing a challenge via the DNS record for the address(es), a challenge via HTTP96 to the DNS address(es), or via some other form of verification to confirm authorization for the DNS address(es).
contents.html_ja: 公開鍵と、証明書のcommon nameまたはsubject alternative nameに含めるドメインネームシステム（DNS）アドレスは、証明書署名要求により、ネットワーク接続を介してRAに提供される。RAは、そのDNSアドレスについて、DNSレコードを介したチャレンジ、DNSアドレスへのHTTP96経由のチャレンジ、またはその他の何らかの検証方法を実施することで、要求者がそのDNSアドレスの証明書を要求する権限を有することを確認する。

contents.html: In cases involving an RA, upon receipt of all information from the requesting entity (e.g., the owner of the new public key), the RA forwards the relevant information to a CA for certification. The RA and CA, in combination, shall perform any validation or other checks required for the algorithm with which the public key will be used (e.g., public-key validation) prior to issuing a certificate. The CA should indicate the checks or validations that will be or have been performed (e.g., in the certificate, the certificate policy, or the certification practice statement). After generation, the certificate is distributed manually or using automated protocols to the RA, the public-key owner or the owner’s representative, or to a certificate repository (i.e., a directory) in accordance with the CA’s certification practice statement.
contents.html_ja: RAを介する場合、要求エンティティ（例：新しい公開鍵の所有者）から全情報を受領したRAは、証明のため関連情報をCAに転送する。証明書発行前に、RAとCAは共同で、公開鍵を使用するアルゴリズムに必要な検証やその他の確認（公開鍵検証など）を実施しなければならない。CAは、実施予定または実施済みの確認・検証を（例：証明書、証明書ポリシー、認証局運用規程で）示すべきである。生成後、証明書は、CAの認証局運用規程に従い、手動または自動プロトコルでRA、公開鍵所有者または所有者の代理人、あるいは証明書リポジトリ（すなわちディレクトリ）へ配布される。

contents.html: 8.1.5.1.1.3 General Distribution of Static Public Keys
contents.html_ja: 8.1.5.1.1.3 静的公開鍵の一般的な配布

contents.html: Static public keys may be distributed to entities other than an RA or CA in several ways. Distribution methods include:
contents.html_ja: 静的公開鍵は、RAやCA以外のエンティティにも複数の方法で配布してよい。配布方法には次がある：

contents.html: Manual distribution of the public key itself by the owner of the public key or the owner’s representative (e.g., in a face-to-face transfer or by a bonded courier): the mandatory assurances listed in Section 8.1.5.1.1 shall be provided to the recipient prior to operational use of the public key.
contents.html_ja: 公開鍵所有者または所有者の代理人が公開鍵自体を手渡しで配布する（例：対面での受け渡し、または身元保証付き運送業者による配送）。この場合、8.1.5.1.1節に列挙する必須保証を、公開鍵の運用上の使用前に受領者に提供しなければならない。

contents.html: 96 HyperText Transfer Protocol
contents.html_ja: 96 HyperText Transfer Protocol

contents.html: Manual (e.g., in a face-to-face transfer or by receipted mail) or automated distribution of a public-key certificate by the public-key owner, the owner’s representative, the CA, or a certificate repository (i.e., a directory): the mandatory assurances listed in Section 8.1.5.1.1 that are not provided by the CA (e.g., public-key validation) shall be provided to or performed by the receiver of the public key prior to the use of the key operationally.
contents.html_ja: 公開鍵所有者、所有者の代理人、CA、または証明書リポジトリ（すなわちディレクトリ）による、公開鍵証明書の手動配布（例：対面での受け渡し、または受領証付き郵便）または自動配布。この場合、8.1.5.1.1節に列挙する必須保証のうちCAが提供しないもの（例：公開鍵検証）は、公開鍵の運用上の使用前に、公開鍵の受領者に提供されるか、受領者が実施しなければならない。

contents.html: Automated distribution of a public key (e.g., using a communication protocol with authentication and content integrity): the mandatory assurances listed in Section 8.1.5.1.1 shall be provided to the receiving entity prior to operational use of the public key.
contents.html_ja: 公開鍵の自動配布（例：認証およびコンテンツ完全性を備える通信プロトコルの使用）。この場合、8.1.5.1.1節に列挙する必須保証を、公開鍵の運用上の使用前に受信エンティティに提供しなければならない。

contents.html: 8.1.5.1.2 Distribution of Ephemeral Public Keys
contents.html_ja: 8.1.5.1.2 エフェメラル公開鍵の配布

contents.html: When used, ephemeral public keys are distributed as part of a secure key-agreement protocol. The key-agreement process (i.e., the key-agreement scheme + the protocol + key confirmation + any associated negotiation + local processing) should provide a recipient with the assurances listed in Section 8.1.5.1.1. The recipient of an ephemeral public key shall obtain assurance of validity of that key as specified in SP 800-56A prior to using that key for subsequent steps in the key-agreement process.
contents.html_ja: エフェメラル公開鍵を使用する場合、それはセキュアな鍵合意プロトコルの一部として配布される。鍵合意プロセス（すなわち、鍵合意方式＋プロトコル＋鍵確認＋関連するネゴシエーション＋ローカル処理）は、8.1.5.1.1節に列挙する保証を受信者に提供すべきである。エフェメラル公開鍵の受信者は、鍵合意プロセスの後続の手順でその鍵を使用する前に、SP 800-56Aの規定に従ってその鍵の正当性の保証を得なければならない。

contents.html: 8.1.5.1.3 Distribution of Centrally Generated Key Pairs
contents.html_ja: 8.1.5.1.3 集中生成鍵ペアの配布

contents.html: When a static key pair is centrally generated, the key pair shall be generated within a FIPS 140-validated cryptographic module or obtained from another source approved by the U.S. Government for protecting national security information for subsequent delivery to the intended owner of the key pair. A signing key pair generated by a central key-generation facility for its subscribers will not provide strong support for non-repudiation for those individual subscribers; therefore, when support for non-repudiation is required, the subscribers should generate their own signing key pairs. However, if the central key-generation facility generates signing key pairs for its own organization and distributes them to members of the organization, then support for non-repudiation may be provided at an organizational level (but not an individual level).
contents.html_ja: 静的鍵ペアを集中生成する場合、鍵ペアは、FIPS 140認証済み暗号モジュール内で生成するか、国家安全保障情報の保護について米国政府が承認した他の供給元から入手し、その後に鍵ペアの所有予定者に引き渡さなければならない。集中鍵生成施設が加入者のために生成した署名鍵ペアは、個々の加入者について否認防止を強く支援するものにはならない。そのため、否認防止の支援が必要な場合は、加入者が自ら署名鍵ペアを生成すべきである。ただし、集中鍵生成施設が自組織のために署名鍵ペアを生成し、組織の構成員に配布する場合は、組織レベルでは（個人レベルではないが）否認防止の支援を提供できる。

contents.html: The private key of a key pair generated at a central facility shall only be distributed to the intended owner of the key pair or to the owner’s representative for subsequent installation. The confidentiality of the centrally generated private key shall be protected, and the procedures for distribution shall include an authentication of the recipient’s identity and authorization as established during entity registration (see Section 8.1.1).
contents.html_ja: 集中施設で生成した鍵ペアの秘密鍵は、鍵ペアの所有予定者、または後でインストールを行う所有者の代理人にのみ配布しなければならない。集中生成した秘密鍵の機密性を保護しなければならず、配布手順には、エンティティ登録時に確立した受信者の識別情報と認可の認証を含めなければならない（8.1.1節を参照）。

contents.html: The key pair may be distributed to the intended owner or owner’s representative using an appropriate manual method (e.g., courier, mail, or other method specified by the key-generation facility) or secure automated method (e.g., a secure communication protocol). The private key shall be distributed in the same manner as a symmetric key (see Section 8.1.5.2.2). The distribution of the public key of a key pair is discussed in Section 8.1.5.1.1.3. During the distribution process, each key of the key pair shall be provided with the appropriate protections for that key (see Section 6.1).
contents.html_ja: 鍵ペアは、適切な手動の方法（例えば、クーリエ、郵送、または鍵生成施設が指定するその他の方法）またはセキュアな自動化された方法（例えば、セキュアな通信プロトコル）を用いて、所有予定者または所有者の代理人に配布してよい。秘密鍵は、対称鍵と同じ方法で配布しなければならない（8.1.5.2.2節を参照）。鍵ペアの公開鍵の配布については8.1.5.1.1.3節で述べる。配布の過程では、鍵ペアの各鍵に、その鍵に適した保護を施さなければならない（6.1節を参照）。

contents.html: Upon receipt of the key pair, the owner shall obtain assurance of the validity of the public key (see SP 800-56A, SP 800-56B, and SP 800-89). The owner shall obtain assurance that the public and private keys of the key pair are correctly associated (i.e., check that they are a consistent pair, for example, by checking that a key encrypted under a public key-transport key can be decrypted by the corresponding private key-transport key).
contents.html_ja: 鍵ペアを受け取った所有者は、公開鍵の正当性の保証を得なければならない（SP 800-56A、SP 800-56BおよびSP 800-89を参照）。所有者は、鍵ペアの公開鍵と秘密鍵が正しく対応していることの保証を得なければならない（すなわち、両者が整合したペアであることを確認する。例えば、公開鍵輸送鍵で暗号化した鍵を、対応する秘密鍵輸送鍵で復号できることを確認する）。

contents.html: 8.1.5.2 Generation and Distribution of Symmetric Keys
contents.html_ja: 8.1.5.2 共通鍵の生成と配布

contents.html: The symmetric keys used for the encryption and decryption of data or other keys and for the computation of MACs (see Sections 4.2.2 and 4.2.3) shall be determined by an approved method and shall be provided with protection that is consistent with Section 6.
contents.html_ja: データまたは他の鍵の暗号化・復号、およびMACの計算（4.2.2節および4.2.3節を参照）に用いる対称鍵は、承認された方法で決定し、6節に整合する保護を施さなければならない。

contents.html: Symmetric keys shall be:
contents.html_ja: 対称鍵は、次のとおりでなければならない。

contents.html: Generated and subsequently distributed (see Sections 8.1.5.2.1 and 8.1.5.2.2) either manually (see Section 8.1.5.2.2.1), using a public key-transport mechanism (see Section 8.1.5.2.2.2), or using a previously distributed or agreed-upon key wrapping key (see Section 8.1.5.2.2.2);
contents.html_ja: 生成後に配布する（8.1.5.2.1節および8.1.5.2.2節を参照）。配布は、手動（8.1.5.2.2.1節を参照）、公開鍵鍵転送方式（8.1.5.2.2.2節を参照）、または事前に配布済みもしくは合意済みの鍵ラッピング鍵（8.1.5.2.2.2節を参照）を用いて行う。

contents.html: Established using a key-agreement scheme (i.e., the generation and distribution are accomplished with one process) (see Section 8.1.5.2.3; or
contents.html_ja: 鍵合意方式を用いて確立する（すなわち、生成と配布を1つのプロセスで行う）（8.1.5.2.3節を参照）。または

contents.html: Derived from a master key/key-derivation key (see Section 8.2.4).
contents.html_ja: マスター鍵／鍵導出鍵から導出する（8.2.4節参照）。

contents.html: 8.1.5.2.1 Key Generation

Symmetric keys shall be either generated by an approved method (e.g., using an approved random number generator; see SP 800-133) or derived from a master key/key-derivation key (see Section 8.2.4) using an approved key-derivation function (see SP 800-108). Symmetric keys may also be generated using key-agreement techniques (see Section 8.1.5.2.3); in this case, a separate key-distribution process is not required (e.g., see SP 800-56A and SP 800-56B).
contents.html_ja: 対称鍵は、承認された方法で生成する（例えば、承認された乱数生成器を用いる。SP 800-133を参照）か、承認された鍵導出関数（SP 800-108を参照）を用いてマスター鍵／鍵導出鍵（8.2.4節を参照）から導出しなければならない。対称鍵は鍵合意技術（8.1.5.2.3節を参照）を用いて生成してもよい。その場合、別途の鍵配布プロセスは不要である（例えば、SP 800-56AおよびSP 800-56Bを参照）。

contents.html: When split-knowledge procedures are used, the key shall only exist outside of a FIPS 140 cryptographic module as multiple key shares. The key may be created within a cryptographic module and then split into shares for export from the module or may be created as separate shares. Each key share shall provide no knowledge of the key value (e.g., each key share must appear to be generated randomly). If knowledge of k shares is required to construct the original key, then knowledge of any k−1 key shares shall provide no information about the original key other than, possibly, its length. Note: A suitable combination function is not provided by simple concatenation (e.g., it is not acceptable to form a 128-bit key by concatenating two 64-bit key shares).
contents.html_ja: 知識分割手順を用いる場合、鍵はFIPS 140暗号モジュールの外部では複数の鍵シェアとしてのみ存在しなければならない。鍵は、暗号モジュール内で作成した後にモジュールから出力するためにシェアに分割してもよいし、最初から個別のシェアとして作成してもよい。各鍵シェアは鍵の値について何の知識も与えてはならない（例えば、各鍵シェアはランダムに生成されたように見えなければならない）。元の鍵を構成するのにk個のシェアの知識が必要である場合、任意のk−1個の鍵シェアの知識は、元の鍵について、場合によってはその長さを除き、何の情報も与えてはならない。注：単純な連結は適切な結合関数ではない（例えば、2つの64ビット鍵シェアを連結して128ビット鍵を作ることは許容されない）。

contents.html: All keys and key shares shall be generated within a FIPS 140-validated cryptographic module or obtained from another source approved by the U.S. Government for the protection of national security information.
contents.html_ja: すべての鍵と鍵シェアは、FIPS 140認証済み暗号モジュール内で生成するか、国家安全保障情報の保護について米国政府が承認した他の供給元から入手しなければならない。

contents.html: 8.1.5.2.2 Key Distribution

Keys generated in accordance with Section 8.1.5.2.1 as key-wrapping keys (i.e., key-encrypting keys), as master/key-derivation keys to be used for key derivation, or for the protection of communicated information are distributed manually (manual key transport) or using an automated key-transport protocol (automated key transport).
contents.html_ja: 8.1.5.2.1節に従って、鍵ラッピング鍵（すなわち鍵暗号化鍵）として、鍵導出に用いるマスター鍵／鍵導出鍵として、または通信される情報の保護のために生成した鍵は、手動（手動鍵輸送）または自動化された鍵輸送プロトコル（自動鍵輸送）を用いて配布される。

contents.html: Keys used only for the storage of information (i.e., data or keying material) shall not be distributed except for backup or to other authorized entities that may require access to the stored information protected by the keys.
contents.html_ja: 情報（すなわちデータまたは鍵材料）の保管にのみ用いる鍵は、バックアップの場合、またはその鍵で保護された保管情報へのアクセスを必要としうる他の認可されたエンティティに配布する場合を除き、配布してはならない。

contents.html: 8.1.5.2.2.1 Manual Key Distribution

Keys and key shares that are distributed manually (i.e., by other than an automated key-transport protocol) shall be protected throughout the distribution process. During manual distribution, secret keys, private keys, and key shares shall either be wrapped (i.e., encrypted with integrity protection) or distributed using appropriate physical security procedures.

contents.html: If split-knowledge procedures are used for key distribution (i.e., a key is distributed as key shares; see Section 8.1.5.2.1), each key share shall be distributed separately to its intended recipient.

contents.html: The process for the manual distribution of secret keys, private keys, and key shares (i.e., secret keying material) shall assure that:

contents.html: The keying material is distributed by an authorized source,
contents.html_ja: 鍵素材は権限を持つ情報源が配布する。

contents.html: Any entity distributing plaintext keying material is trusted by both the entity that generates the keying material and any entity that receives the keying material,
contents.html_ja: 平文の鍵素材を配布する主体は、生成主体と受領主体の双方から信頼されている。

contents.html: The keying material is protected in accordance with Section 6, and
contents.html_ja: 鍵素材は6節に従って保護される。

contents.html: The keying material is received by the authorized recipient(s).
contents.html_ja: 鍵素材は権限を持つ受領者が受け取る。

contents.html: When distributed in encrypted form, the key or key share shall be encrypted using an approved key-wrapping scheme and a key-wrapping key that is used only for key wrapping or using an approved key-transport scheme and a public key-transport key owned by the intended recipient. The key-wrapping key or public key-transport key shall have been distributed as specified in this Recommendation.

Physical security procedures may be used for all forms of manual key distribution. However, these procedures are particularly critical when the secret keying material is distributed in plaintext form. In addition to the assurances listed above, accountability and auditing of the distribution process should be used (see Sections 9.3 and 9.4).
8.1.5.2.2.2 Automated Key Distribution/Key Transport/Key Wrapping
contents.html_ja: 8.1.5.2.2.2 自動鍵配布／鍵転送／鍵ラッピング

contents.html: Automated key distribution may be used to distribute secret keys, private keys, and key shares via a communication channel (e.g., the internet). This requires the distribution/establishment of a key-wrapping key (i.e., a key-encryption key) or a public key-transport key as follows:
A key-wrapping key shall be generated and distributed in accordance with Sections 8.1.5.2.1 and 8.1.5.2.2 or established using a key-establishment scheme as defined in Section 8.1.5.2.3.
contents.html_ja: 鍵ラッピング鍵は、8.1.5.2.1節および8.1.5.2.2節に従って生成して配布するか、8.1.5.2.3節に定義する鍵確立方式を用いて確立しなければならない。

contents.html: A public key-transport key shall be generated and distributed as specified in Section 8.1.5.1.
contents.html_ja: 公開鍵転送鍵は、8.1.5.1節に規定されるとおり生成・配布しなければならない（shall）。

contents.html: Only approved key-wrapping or public key-transport schemes shall be used. The approved schemes provide assurance that:

a. For symmetric key-wrapping schemes: The key-wrapping key and the distributed keying material are not disclosed or modified. Approved key-wrapping methods that provide both confidentiality and integrity protection are provided in SP 800-38F.97

For asymmetric key-transport schemes: The private key-transport key and the distributed keying material are not disclosed or modified, and correct association between the private and public key-transport keys is maintained. Approved key-transport schemes using asymmetric techniques are discussed in SP 800-56A and SP 800-56B.

contents.html: c. The keying material is protected in accordance with Section 6.

column_reflow.proof_note: item c is printed after item b (continued) and before 'In addition'

contents.html: In addition, the approved schemes, together with the associated key-establishment protocol, should provide the following assurances:

column_reflow.proof_note: 'In addition, the approved schemes...' is printed after item c, not before it

contents.html: 97 SP 800-38F, Recommendation for Block Cipher Modes of Operation: Methods for Key Wrapping.
d. Each entity in the key-distribution process knows the identifier associated with the other entity(ies),
e. The keying material is correctly associated with the entities involved in the key-distribution process, and
f. The keying material has been received correctly (e.g., using a key-confirmation method).
8.1.5.2.3 Key Agreement

Key agreement is used in a communication environment to establish keying material using information contributed by all entities in the communication (most commonly by only two entities) without actually sending the keying material. Only approved key-agreement schemes shall be used. Approved key-agreement schemes using asymmetric techniques are provided in SP 800-56A and SP 800-56B. These key-agreement schemes use asymmetric key pairs to calculate shared secrets, which are then used to derive symmetric keys and other keying material (e.g., IVs).

A key-agreement scheme uses either static or ephemeral asymmetric key pairs or both. The asymmetric key pairs should be generated and distributed as discussed in Section 8.1.5.1. Keying material derived using a key-agreement scheme shall be protected as specified in Section 6.
A key-agreement scheme and its associated key-establishment protocol should provide the following assurances:

1. The identifiers for entities involved in the key-establishment protocol are correctly associated with those entities. Assurance for the association of identifiers to entities may be achieved by the key-agreement scheme or may be achieved by the protocol in which key agreement is performed. Note that the identifier may be a “pseudo-identifier” (a pseudonym) – not, for example, the identifier appearing on the entity’s birth certificate.

In the general case, an identifier is associated with each entity involved in the key-establishment protocol, and each entity must be able to associate all the other entities with their appropriate identifiers. In special cases, such as the secure distribution of public information on a website, the association with an identifier may only be required for a subset of the entities (e.g., only the server).
The keys used in the key-agreement scheme are correctly associated with the entities involved in the key-establishment process.
contents.html_ja: 鍵共有方式で用いる鍵は、鍵確立プロセスの関係主体と正しく関連付けられている。

contents.html: The derived keying material is correct (e.g., using a key-confirmation method).
contents.html_ja: 導出された鍵素材が正しい（例：鍵確認方式を使用する）。

contents.html: Keying material derived through key agreement and its enabling protocol shall not be used to protect and send information until the three assurances described above have been obtained.
contents.html_ja: 鍵共有およびその実現プロトコルを通じて導出された鍵素材は、上記3つの保証が得られるまで情報保護・送信に使用してはならない（shall not）。

contents.html: 8.1.5.3 Generation and Distribution of Other Keying Material
contents.html_ja: 8.1.5.3 その他の鍵素材の生成と配布

contents.html: Keys are often generated in conjunction with or are used with other keying material. This other keying material shall be protected in accordance with Section 6.2. Table 6 specifies the type(s) of protection required for keying material other than keys.
contents.html_ja: 鍵は、他の鍵素材とともに、または他の鍵素材に関連して生成されることや、他の鍵素材とともに使用されることが多い。この他の鍵素材は、6.2節に従って保護しなければならない。表6は、鍵以外の鍵素材に必要な保護の種類を示す。

contents.html: 8.1.5.3.1 Domain Parameters
contents.html_ja: 8.1.5.3.1 ドメインパラメータ

contents.html: Domain parameters are used by some public-key algorithms to generate key pairs, compute digital signatures, or establish keys. Typically, domain parameters are generated infrequently and used by a community of entities for a substantial period of time. Domain parameters may be distributed in the same manner as the public keys with which they are associated, or they may be made available at some other accessible site. Assurance of the validity of the domain parameters shall be obtained prior to use − either by a trusted entity that vouches for the parameters (e.g., a CA) or by the entities that use them. Assurance of domain-parameter validity is addressed in SP 800-56A (for key-establishment schemes) and SP 800-89 (for digital signatures). Obtaining this assurance should be addressed in a CA’s certification practices statement or an organization’s security plan.
contents.html_ja: ドメインパラメータは、一部の公開鍵アルゴリズムにおいて、鍵ペアの生成、デジタル署名の計算、または鍵の確立に使用される。通常、ドメインパラメータの生成頻度は低く、エンティティのコミュニティがかなりの期間にわたって使用する。ドメインパラメータは、関連付けられた公開鍵と同じ方法で配布してもよいし、他のアクセス可能なサイトで利用できるようにしてもよい。ドメインパラメータの正当性の保証は、使用に先立って、そのパラメータを保証する信頼できるエンティティ（例えばCA）、またはそれを使用するエンティティのいずれかによって得なければならない。ドメインパラメータの正当性の保証については、SP 800-56A（鍵確立方式の場合）およびSP 800-89（デジタル署名の場合）で扱っている。この保証の取得については、CAの認証実践規程または組織のセキュリティ計画で扱うべきである。

contents.html: 8.1.5.3.2 Initialization Vectors
contents.html_ja: 8.1.5.3.2 初期化ベクトル

contents.html: Initialization vectors (IVs) are used by symmetric-key algorithms in several modes of operation for encryption and decryption, for authentication, or both. The criteria for the generation and use of IVs are provided in the SP 800-38 series of publications; IVs shall be protected as specified in Section 6.1.2. IVs may be distributed in the same manner as their associated keys or may be distributed with the information that uses the IVs as part of the cryptographic mechanism.
contents.html_ja: 初期化ベクトル（IV）は、共通鍵アルゴリズムのいくつかの動作モードで、暗号化と復号、認証、またはその両方に使用される。IVの生成と使用の基準はSP 800-38シリーズの文書に示されている。IVは6.1.2節の規定に従って保護しなければならない。IVは、関連する鍵と同じ方法で配布してもよく、暗号メカニズムの一部としてIVを使用する情報とともに配布してもよい。

contents.html: 8.1.5.3.3 Shared Secrets

Shared secrets are computed during the execution of an asymmetric key-agreement scheme and are subsequently used to derive keying material. Shared secrets are generated as specified by an appropriate key-agreement scheme (see SP 800-56A and SP 800-56B) and shall not be distributed nor used directly as keying material.
contents.html_ja: 共有秘密は非対称鍵共有方式の実行中に計算され、その後鍵素材の導出に使用される。共有秘密は適切な鍵共有方式（SP 800-56AおよびSP 800-56B参照）に規定されるとおり生成され、配布してはならず、また鍵素材として直接使用してはならない（shall not）。

contents.html: 8.1.5.3.4 RBG Seeds
contents.html_ja: 8.1.5.3.4 RBGシード

contents.html: A random bit generator (RBG) is a device or algorithm that outputs a sequence of bits that is unpredictable; RBGs are often called random number generators. Approved RBGs are specified in the SP 800-90 series of publications. RBGs depend on the introduction of truly random bits that are used to generate the seeds that are used to initialize an RBG; these seeds must be kept secret. An initialized RBG is often used to generate keys and other values requiring unpredictability. The seeds themselves shall not be used for any purpose other than as RBG input.
contents.html_ja: ランダムビット生成器（RBG）は、予測不能なビット列を出力する装置またはアルゴリズムであり、乱数生成器と呼ばれることも多い。承認済みRBGはSP 800-90シリーズの文書に規定されている。RBGは、RBGの初期化に使用するシードの生成に使う真にランダムなビットの導入に依存しており、これらのシードは秘密に保たなければならない。初期化されたRBGは、鍵や、予測不能性を必要とするその他の値の生成にしばしば使用される。シード自体は、RBGの入力以外の目的に使用してはならない。

contents.html: 8.1.5.3.5 Other Public and Secret Information
contents.html_ja: 8.1.5.3.5 その他の公開情報および秘密情報

contents.html: Public and secret information may be used during the seeding of an RBG (see Section 8.1.5.3.4) or during the generation or establishment of keying material (see SP 800-56A, SP 800-56B, and SP 800-10898). Public information may be distributed; secret information shall be protected in the same manner as a private or secret key during distribution.
contents.html_ja: 公開情報および秘密情報は、RBGのシード付与（8.1.5.3.4節を参照）の際、または鍵材料の生成もしくは確立（SP 800-56A、SP 800-56B、およびSP 800-10898を参照）の際に使用されることがある。公開情報は配布してもよい。秘密情報は、配布中、私有鍵または秘密鍵と同じ方法で保護しなければならない。

contents.html: 98 SP 800-108, Recommendation for Key Derivation Using Pseudorandom Functions.
contents.html_ja: 98 SP 800-108, Recommendation for Key Derivation Using Pseudorandom Functions.

contents.html: 8.1.5.3.6 Intermediate Results
Intermediate results occur during computation using cryptographic algorithms. These results shall not be distributed as or with the keying material.
contents.html_ja: 暗号アルゴリズムを用いた計算中には中間結果が生じる。これらの結果は、鍵素材として、または鍵素材とともに配布してはならない。

contents.html: 8.1.5.3.7 Random Bits/Numbers
contents.html_ja: 8.1.5.3.7 ランダムビット／数値

contents.html: Random bits (or numbers) are used for many purposes, including the generation of keys and nonces and the issuing of challenges during the execution of communication protocols. Random bits may be distributed, but whether or not confidentiality protection is required depends on the context in which the random bits are used.
contents.html_ja: ランダムビット（または乱数）は、鍵やノンスの生成、通信プロトコルの実行中のチャレンジの発行など、多くの目的に使用される。ランダムビットは配布してもよい（may）が、機密性保護が必要かどうかは、そのランダムビットが使用される状況による。

contents.html: 8.1.5.3.8 Passwords

Passwords are used for identity authentication, authorization, and, in some cases, to derive keying material (see SP 800-132). Passwords may be distributed, but their protection during distribution shall be consistent with the protection required for their use. For example, if the password will be used to access cryptographic keys that are used to provide 128 bits of security strength when protecting data, then the password needs to be provided with at least 128 bits of protection as well. Note that poorly selected passwords alone may not provide the required amount of protection for key access and are potentially the weak point of the process (i.e., it may be far easier to guess the password than to attempt to “break” the cryptographic protection used on the password). It is the responsibility of users and organizations to select passwords that provide the requisite amount of protection for the keys they protect.
contents.html_ja: パスワードは、本人認証、権限付与、場合によっては鍵素材の導出（SP 800-132を参照）に使用される。パスワードを配布してもよいが、配布中の保護は、その使用に必要な保護と整合していなければならない。例えば、データを保護する際に128ビットのセキュリティ強度を提供する暗号鍵へのアクセスにパスワードを使用する場合、パスワードにも少なくとも128ビットの保護を提供する必要がある。なお、不適切に選択されたパスワードだけでは、鍵へのアクセスに必要な保護を提供できない場合があり、処理の弱点となる可能性がある（すなわち、パスワードに用いられる暗号保護を「破る」よりも、パスワードを推測するほうがはるかに容易な場合がある）。保護する鍵に必要な水準の保護を提供するパスワードを選択する責任は、ユーザーと組織にある。

contents.html: 8.1.6 Key Registration Function
contents.html_ja: 8.1.6 鍵登録機能

contents.html: Key registration results in the binding of keying material to information associated with a particular entity. Keys that would be registered include the public key of an asymmetric key pair and the symmetric key used to bootstrap an entity into a system. Normally, keys generated during communications (e.g., using key-agreement schemes or key derivation functions) would not be registered. Information provided during registration typically includes the identifier of the entity associated with the keying material (the owner) and the intended use of the keying material (e.g., as a signing key, data-encryption key, etc.). Additional information may include authorization information, specify a level of trust, or indicate where the key is stored (e.g., its physical location, internet address, or device identity). The binding is performed after the entity’s identity has been authenticated by a means that is consistent with the system policy (see Section 8.1.1). The binding provides assurance to the community at large that the keying material is used by the correct entity in the correct application. The binding is often cryptographic to create a strong association between the keying material and the entity. A trusted third party performs the binding. Examples of a trusted third party include a Kerberos realm server or a PKI certification authority (CA). Identifiers issued by a trusted third party shall be unique to that party.
contents.html_ja: 鍵の登録により、鍵材料が特定のエンティティに関連付けられた情報に結び付けられる（バインディング）。登録対象となる鍵には、非対称鍵ペアの公開鍵や、エンティティをシステムに初期参加させる（ブートストラップする）ために用いる対称鍵がある。通常、通信中に生成される鍵（例えば、鍵合意方式や鍵導出関数を用いて生成される鍵）は登録されない。登録時に提供される情報には、通常、鍵材料に関連付けられたエンティティ（所有者）の識別子と、鍵材料の使用目的（例えば、署名鍵、データ暗号化鍵など）が含まれる。追加情報として、認可情報を含めたり、信頼レベルを指定したり、鍵の保管場所（例えば、物理的な場所、インターネットアドレス、デバイス識別情報）を示したりすることがある。バインディングは、システムポリシーに整合する手段によってエンティティの識別情報を認証した後に行う（8.1.1節を参照）。バインディングは、鍵材料が正しいエンティティによって正しいアプリケーションで使用されることを、コミュニティ全体に保証する。鍵材料とエンティティを強く関連付けるため、バインディングは暗号技術によることが多い。バインディングは信頼できる第三者が行う。信頼できる第三者の例として、Kerberosレルムサーバや PKI 認証局（CA）がある。信頼できる第三者が発行する識別子は、その第三者内で一意でなければならない。

contents.html: When a Kerberos realm server performs the binding, a symmetric key is stored on the server with the corresponding metadata. In this case, the registered keying material is maintained in secure storage (i.e., the keys are provided with confidentiality and integrity protection).
contents.html_ja: Kerberosレルムサーバがバインディングを行う場合、対称鍵は対応するメタデータとともにサーバに保管される。この場合、登録された鍵材料はセキュアな記憶域で維持される（すなわち、鍵には機密性と完全性の保護が施される）。

contents.html: When a CA performs the binding, the public key and associated information (e.g., domain parameters and some metadata, often called attributes) are placed in a public-key certificate that is digitally signed by the CA. In this case, the registered keying material may be made publicly available.
contents.html_ja: CAがバインディングを行う場合、公開鍵と関連情報（例えば、ドメインパラメータや、しばしば属性と呼ばれる一部のメタデータ）は、CAがデジタル署名した公開鍵証明書に格納される。この場合、登録された鍵材料を一般に公開してもよい。

contents.html: When a CA provides a certificate for a public key, the public key shall be verified to ensure that it is associated with the private key known by the purported owner of the public key. This provides assurance of possession, also known as proof of possession (POP). When POP is used to obtain assurance of possession, the assurance shall be accomplished as specified in Section 8.1.5.1.1.2.
contents.html_ja: CAが公開鍵の証明書を発行する場合、その公開鍵が、公開鍵の所有者とされる者が知る秘密鍵に対応していることを確認しなければならない。これにより所有の保証（所有証明（POP）とも呼ばれる）が得られる。所有の保証を得るためにPOPを用いる場合、その保証は8.1.5.1.1.2節の規定に従って得なければならない。

contents.html: Registered keys and certificates shall be included in an inventory (see Section 9.2).
contents.html_ja: 登録された鍵と証明書は、インベントリに含めなければならない（9.2節を参照）。

contents.html: 8.2 Operational Phase
contents.html_ja: 8.2 運用フェーズ

contents.html: Keying material used during the cryptoperiod of a key is often stored for access as needed. During storage, the keying material and other key information shall be protected as specified in Section 6.2.2. During normal use, the key information is stored either in the device or module that uses that information or on an immediately accessible storage media. The keying material is acquired from storage when required for operational use and not present in active memory within the device or module.
contents.html_ja: 鍵の暗号期間中に使用する鍵材料は、必要に応じてアクセスできるよう保管されることが多い。保管中、鍵材料およびその他の鍵情報は6.2.2節の規定に従って保護しなければならない。通常の使用時には、鍵情報は、その情報を使用するデバイスもしくはモジュール内、または即時にアクセス可能な記憶媒体に保管される。鍵材料は、運用上の使用に必要になったときに、デバイスまたはモジュール内のアクティブメモリに存在しない場合に記憶域から取得される。

contents.html: To provide continuity of operations when the keying material becomes unavailable for use from normal operational storage during its cryptoperiod (e.g., because the material is lost or corrupted), keying material may need to be recoverable. If an analysis of system operations indicates that the keying material needs to be recoverable, then the keying material shall either be backed up (see Section 8.2.2.1), archived (see Section 8.3.1), or the system shall be designed to allow reconstruction (e.g., re-derivation) of the keying material. Retrieving or reconstructing keying material from an archive or backup is commonly known as key recovery (see Section 8.2.2.2).
contents.html_ja: 暗号期間中に鍵材料が通常の運用記憶域から使用できなくなった場合（例えば、鍵材料の紛失や破損による）に業務の継続性を確保するため、鍵材料を復旧可能にしておく必要がある場合がある。システム運用の分析により鍵材料を復旧可能にする必要があると判断された場合、鍵材料をバックアップする（8.2.2.1節を参照）か、アーカイブする（8.3.1節を参照）か、または鍵材料の再構成（例えば再導出）が可能なようにシステムを設計しなければならない。アーカイブまたはバックアップから鍵材料を取り出すこと、または鍵材料を再構成することは、一般に鍵の復旧と呼ばれる（8.2.2.2節を参照）。

contents.html: At the end of a key’s cryptoperiod, a new key needs to be available to replace the old key if operations are to continue. This can be accomplished by re-keying (see Section 8.2.3.1) or by key derivation (see Section 8.2.4). A key should be destroyed as soon as that key is no longer needed in order to reduce the risk of exposure; when destroyed, the key shall be destroyed in accordance with Section 8.3.4.
contents.html_ja: 鍵の暗号期間が終了する時点で業務を継続するには、古い鍵を置き換える新しい鍵を使用可能にしておく必要がある。これは、鍵の再生成（8.2.3.1節を参照）または鍵導出（8.2.4節を参照）によって実現できる。露出のリスクを低減するため、鍵は不要になり次第破棄すべきである。破棄する場合は、8.3.4節に従って破棄しなければならない。

contents.html: 8.2.1 Normal Operational Storage Function
contents.html_ja: 8.2.1 通常運用時の保存機能

contents.html: One objective of key management is to facilitate the operational availability of keying material for standard cryptographic purposes. Usually, a key remains operational until the end of the key’s cryptoperiod (i.e., the expiration date). During normal operational use, keying material is available in the device or module (e.g., in RAM) or in an immediately accessible storage media (e.g., on a local hard disk).
contents.html_ja: 鍵管理の目的の1つは、標準的な暗号用途に使用する鍵素材を運用可能な状態に保つことである。通常、鍵は鍵の暗号期間の終了（すなわち有効期限）まで運用状態にある。通常の運用中、鍵素材は装置やモジュール内（例：RAM）、または直ちにアクセス可能な記憶媒体（例：ローカルのハードディスク）上で利用可能である。

contents.html: 8.2.1.1 Cryptographic Module Storage
contents.html_ja: 8.2.1.1 暗号モジュール内の保存

contents.html: Keying material may be stored in the cryptographic module that adds, checks, or removes the cryptographic protection on information. The storage of the keying material shall be consistent with Section 6.2.2 as well as with FIPS 140.
contents.html_ja: 鍵素材は、情報の暗号保護を追加・検査・除去する暗号モジュール内に保存してもよい（may）。保存は6.2.2節およびFIPS 140に整合しなければならない（shall）。

contents.html: 8.2.1.2 Immediately Accessible Storage Media
contents.html_ja: 8.2.1.2 すぐにアクセス可能な記憶媒体

contents.html: Keying material may need to be stored for normal cryptographic operations on an immediately accessible storage media (e.g., a local hard drive) during the cryptoperiod of the key. The storage requirements of Section 6.2.2 shall apply to this keying material.
contents.html_ja: 鍵素材は、鍵の暗号期間中、通常の暗号処理のために、直ちにアクセス可能な記憶媒体（例：ローカルのハードドライブ）に保存する必要がある場合がある。この鍵素材には、6.2.2節の保管要件を適用しなければならない。

contents.html: 8.2.2 Continuity of Operations Function
contents.html_ja: 8.2.2 運用継続機能

contents.html: Keying material can become lost or unusable due to hardware damage, corruption or loss of program or data files, system policy, or configuration changes. In order to maintain continuity, it is often necessary for users and/or administrators to be able to recover keying materials from backup storage. However, if operations can be continued without the backup of keying material (e.g., by re-keying) or the keying material can be recovered or reconstructed without being saved, it may be preferable not to save the keying material in order to lessen the possibility of a compromise of the keying material or other cryptographically related information.

column_reflow.proof_note: 'Keying material can become lost...' continues at the top of the page and precedes the 'compromise' paragraph

contents.html: The compromise of keying material affects the continuity of operations (see Section 8.4). When keying material is compromised, continuity of operations requires the establishment of entirely new keying material (see Section 8.1.5) following an assessment of the keying material that was affected; all affected keying material needs to be replaced.

column_reflow.proof_note: 'The compromise of keying material...' is not printed on page 117; it is on page 118 after the 'Keying material can become lost' paragraph; 'The compromise...' paragraph is printed after 'Keying material can become lost...' (block 2)

contents.html: 8.2.2.1 Backup Storage
contents.html_ja: 8.2.2.1 バックアップ保存

contents.html: The backup of keying material on an independent, secure storage media provides a source for key recovery (see Section 8.2.2.2). Backup storage is used to store copies of key information that is also currently available in normal operational storage during a key’s cryptoperiod (i.e., in the cryptographic module or on an immediately accessible storage media; see Section 8.2.1.1). Not all keys need to be backed up. The storage requirements of Section 6.2.2 apply to keying material that is backed up. Tables 7 and 8 provide guidance about the backup of each type of keying material and other related information. An “OK” indicates that storage is permissible but not necessarily required. The final determination for backup should be made based on the application in which the keying material is used. A detailed discussion about the backup of each type of key and other key information is provided in Appendix B.3.

Keying material maintained in backup storage should remain in storage for at least as long as the same keying material is maintained for normal operational use (see Section 8.2.1). When no longer needed for normal operational use, the keying material and other related information should be removed from backup storage. When removed from backup storage, all traces of the information in backup storage shall be destroyed in accordance with Section 8.3.4.
A discussion of backup and recovery is provided in [ITL Bulletin].99
